Edited by Emmanuel Gonzalez

Some links on this page are affiliate links. Affiliate disclosure.

Audio is not stated on that row. The official Kling API is $0.084/s at 720p without audio, or $0.126/s at 720p with audio. How does this comparison work?

This page compares Kling 3.0 bought on Higgsfield with Kling bought direct. A Higgsfield credit-plan figure uses the official (or official-estimate) credits per clip and the plan’s dollars and credits, and it holds only if you use the credits you pay for. Official API rows are published dollar rates per second of output. Official app plans are shown as dollars and credits per month, not as $/s, when credits per clip are unpublished.

    What do official Kling plans and Higgsfield plans cost?

    On Nov 14, 2026 PT, the official membership page listed a $0 Basic plan with no monthly credits, then Standard, Pro, Premier, and Ultra+. Standard was $6.99 for the first month, then $8.80 a month (list $10), with 660 credits a month. Yearly Standard was $79.20 (list $120) and grants 660 credits each month for 12 months. Premier lets you pick 8,000, 18,000, 28,000, or 38,000 credits a month. Those membership figures were not re-opened today; see Kling AI pricing and credits for the full tables. Higgsfield’s catalog plans, checked Nov 17, 2026 PT, are Starter $19 a month for 270 credits, Plus $59 monthly or $33 a month billed annually for 1,200 credits, and Ultra $129 monthly or $50 a month billed annually for 3,000 credits. Full official tables: Kling AI pricing and credits. Higgsfield plan math: Higgsfield pricing explained.

    Which option is best for each use?

    Higgsfield Ultra (annual) is best for the lowest Kling 3.0 catalog rate we can show at 720p, if you use every paid credit. It is not for a published official app-plan $/s, because that conversion is unknown, or for buyers who only want the official Kling site and API. The official Kling API is best for a published pay-as-you-go rate with a stated resolution and audio flag. It is not the cheapest catalog route for Kling 3.0 at 720p. No line is given for official Standard or Premier cost per second.

    How do we calculate this?

    Each dollar figure is a current price row, with the vendor page and the date that page was checked. A published rate is a dollars-per-second figure on that page, or an API credit count times the credit price the page states. A credit-plan figure is plan price ÷ credits × credits per clip ÷ seconds, and it assumes every credit you pay for is used. When the vendor marks that count with "~", "roughly", or "estimated", the row is labelled estimated from credit plan and is not a list price. A promo shows its end date when the vendor gave one. The full method is on the about page (https://vidfare.com/about/).
